Subject: Amaya / Redwood - Data retention, SOC 2 & vendor questionnaire follow-up

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- SOC 2 / Compliance: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II for our hosted inference control surface in May 2026. I’ve attached the executive SOC 2 report for your security team to review. If you need the full assertion or contact for our auditor, we can provide that.
- HIPAA/GDPR: We support HIPAA workflows under Dedicated or Private deployments and are happy to execute a BAA for those customers. For hosted API usage, please let me know if PHI will be in requests so we can review deployment options.
- Vendor security questionnaire: I’m attaching our vendor questionnaire for Amaya to review and (if helpful) we can take an initial pass on some items to speed things up.
- Data retention / deletion SLAs: One callout from the demo — please confirm Amaya’s desired retention windows for user content, logs, and backups. Our standard defaults are: primary data deletions processed within 30 days, backups/snapshots retained up to 90 days before permanent purge, and requestable log exports retained 90 days by default (configurable).

Next steps
- Emily: Can you initiate the vendor security questionnaire (attached) and loop in security-ops@amayahealth.com and procurement?
- Marissa / Neha: We’ll send the SOC 2 executive report and a Data Retention SLA matrix (attached) with more detail on backups and snapshot lifecycle.
- If useful, happy to set a 30-min call next week with our security lead (Neha) to walk through the attestation and retention mechanics.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole

Is there an additional retention window for immutable snapshots or disaster recovery copies?

I’ve attached our partially completed vendor questionnaire to start (the team filled the high-level org items). I looped security-ops so they have visibility. Procurement will step in next for contract/BAA once security signs off.

Emily —

Thanks — answered inline below and attaching the SLA matrix for clarity. Neha (cc) from our InfoSec team will join the call if you want to review in more detail.

- SOC 2 coverage: The attached SOC 2 Type II (May 2026) covers Redwood’s hosted inference control surface and our control environment for API serving, authentication, and logging. Dedicated and Private deployments are listed in scope for configuration and deployment controls; if you require the auditor’s letter specific to an on-prem or VPC package, we can obtain the supplemental auditor confirmation.

- HIPAA / BAA: Redwood will execute a BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted (multi-tenant) API usage is not covered under our standard BAA unless scoped and contracted as part of an enterprise Dedicated offering. We’ll have procurement coordinate any custom language.

- Deletion SLA for primary data:
  * Customer-initiated deletion requests are queued and processed within 30 calendar days for primary datasets (application data, embeddings, prompt logs) by default. We can contract tighter SLAs for enterprise deals (e.g., 14 days) as part of Dedicated commitments.

- Backups, snapshots and offsite copies:
  * Backups & snapshots: point-in-time snapshots are retained for up to 90 days by default. When a primary-data deletion is processed, we mark the data for blocker removal and schedule snapshot purges. Snapshot purge window is up to an additional 60 days to allow for safe recovery and replication reconciliation (so effective maximum is ~150 days unless otherwise contracted).
  * Immutable/archival copies: we do not create indefinite immutable archives for customer data by default. If Amaya requires long-term immutable archives for regulatory reasons, we’ll need to capture that in the contract and define retention/escape clauses.
  * Offsite replication: backups are replicated across availability zones; offsite disaster recovery copies are encrypted and follow the same purge lifecycle unless otherwise requested.

- Encryption & access controls: All backups and snapshots are encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS keys for Dedicated / Private. For hosted customers we encrypt with our KMS; we offer CMK/HSM integrations for enterprise contracts. Access to backup storage is restricted to a small set of operations engineers and logged via audit trails.

- Log retention: Application and access logs default to 90 days retention. We can extend to 12+ months for compliance needs; logs are retained separately from customer datasets and can be delivered as exports on request.

Attachments included:

- Redwood_Data_Retention_SLA_matrix.xlsx
